paragraphs: TT AVlNG vanquished Yama, the foremost of celestials, Havana delighting in warfare, saw his adherents. And seeing Havana, with* his. person bathed in blood, bettered by the weapon discharged at him, they were seized with surprise. And hailing him with victory, the councillors headed by Maricha, having been encouraged by Havana, ascended Pushpaka. And then the Raksha entered the regeon of waters — ^the abode of Daityas and serpents, well protected by Varuna. And arriving at Bhogavati — the city governed by Vasuki, he brought the serpents under subjection and then, delighted, bent his course to the palace — Manimayi. There dwelt the Nivatakavachas, who had obtained boons. Those Daityas were possessed of prowess and endowed with strength, — carrying various weapons, breathing high spirits and invincible in battle.

And the Danavas and Rakshasas growing enragjiid fell to raving each other with darts and tridents, Kuli^as and axes send patti^as. And as they faught one entire year passed away and neither side obtained victory or was worsted. And then that way of the triune sphere, that God, the undeteriorating Great-father, swiftly presented himself on the scene mounted on his excellent car. And making the Nivatakavachas desist from battle the ancient great-father spake in clear words — 'Even the celestials and the Asuras arc not abje to vanquish this Ravana in battle ; nor can the Danavas backed by the gods can destroy you. Do you therefore turn your minds to making friends with the Rakshasa, All interests are forsooth the common possession of friends.’

Thereat Ravana made friends with the Nivatakavachas in the presence of Fire ; and then rejoiced greatly. And duly honored (by them) Da9anana passed there a year, without any feeling of that place being different from his own home ; and spent his time agreeably. And having learnt there an hundred sorts of illusion, he directed his course to Rasatala, searching for the city of the lord of waters. And then going to the city named Agma ruled by the Kalakayas, (Ravana) slew the Kalakayas endowed with terrific striength ; and then with his sword cut off his brother.in-law,* * * § the husband of Surpanakha, the mighty Vidyutjibha possessed of terrific strength ; as that R§,kshasa in the encounter was licking (the limbs of Ravana’s followers). f Having vanquished him, he, in a moment, destroyed four hundred Daityas.

And then the lord of Rakshasas saw the grand abode of Varuna resembling a mass of white clouds, and effulgent like unto Kaila^a itself ; — and also saw the milk-codserving Surabhi stationed there ; from the streams of whose milk was produced the ocean named Kshiroda.| And there Ravana saw the mother of kinc and the foremost of bulls ; from whom springeth that maker of night the mild-beaming-moon ; taking refuge under whom subsist the prime saints and those living on froth, the frolh§ (of milk) ; and wherefrom sprang ambrosia as well as the Svvadha of Svvadhasubsisting ones^, even her that goeth with human beings under the name of Surabhi. Having gone round this r This explanation is the commentator's. t Lit, the 4a of milk. § A typical instance of the lengths which the self-denial of the Hindu sages went is furnished by the case of a certain class of ascetics, who, ab.staining from every other kind of food, lived solely on the froth of milk, falling off from the udders after the calf had drunk it.

This fiulh-drinking, in preference to drinking the milk itself was dictated by a motive of charity — vi/., The ancestral manes. RAM AY AN A, wonderful (cow), RSvana entered the exceedingly dreadful abode of Varuna) guarded by various kinds of forces. And then he beheld Varuna’s splendid mansion, streaming with hundreds of torrents, resembling a mass of autumnal clouds, and always wearing a delightful aspect. And killing the generals of the forces, after having been resisted by them, he addressed the warriors, saying, — ‘Do you speedily acquaint your king with this “ Ravana hath come here seeking battle.” Do thou give him fight, qr say with joined hands, ‘I have been defeated by thee, and then thou hast no fear whatever ?’

In the meantime the sons and grandsons of the high-souled Varuna, as well as those of Pushkara issued forth. And they, endowed with every virtue, accompanied by their own forces, yoked cars furnished with the effulgence of the rising Sun, and coursing at the desire of their riders. And then there took place a mighty encounter capable of making people’s down stand on end, between the sons of the lord of waters, and those of the intelligent RSvana, And in a short while that entire host of Varuna was brought down by the highly powerful councillor of that Rakshasa Da9agriva, And seeing their own forces brought to straits in the conflict and driven back in the fight with networks of shafts, and down on the ground and seeing Ravana in Pushpaka, Varuna’s sons swiftly shot into the welkin with their fleet-footing cars.

And after they had attained a station of equal vantage (with R&vana) in the sky,* great was the encounter that then took place in the shy, resembling the encounter of the deities and the Danavas. And turning away,. RSvana in the conflict by means of shafts resembling fire, they, exceedingly rejoiced, emitted various shouts. And then Mahodara, eoeraged on seeing the king sore pressed, casting on the earth. off fear, and wrought up w'ith rage, began to go around, eager for fight. And smit with his mace by Mahodara, Varuna’s sons coursing at will and resembling the wind (in velocity), dropped down to the ground. And having slain those warriors and also those horses of Varuna’s sons (Mahodara) seeing them lying down deprived of their cars swiftly sent up a tremendous cheer.

And destroyed by Mahodara, their cars and horses together w'ith their fore^ most charioteers, lay low on the earth. And then forsaking their cars, the sons of the high-souled Varuna, stationed in the sky, did not experience any pain* by virtue of their native power. And having stretched their bow's they pierced Mahodara, and then, all together they greatly angered prevented Ravana. As the clouds, with a thousand torrents cleave a mountain, so they, with dreadful shafts, resembling thunderbolts and discharged off the bows, pierced him. Thereupon the Ten-nccked (demon), excited with w’rath like the fire of dcssolution, pierced them to their very vitals with highly dreadful arrows. And stationed above, he showered on them variegated maces, Valldsf Pditicas, saktis and huge Sataghms.

Thereupon with the arrow’s the infantry were greatly exhausted like unto young elephants six years old, fallen in mire. Beholding Varuna’s sons thus worn out and overwhelmed the highly powerful Ravana roared in delight like unto clouds. Thereupon emitting loud cries the Rakshaha, like unto a cloud, w’ith a downpour of diverse shafts, destroyed the offspring of Varuna. Thereupon they were all deh'ated and fell dead on the ground and all their followers (led away from the field of battle to their homes. Ravana spoke unto them. — “ Do ye communicate this to t An arrow with a ceresent-shaped head. RAMAVANA. Varuna.” Whereto his minister Prahasta replied unto Rivana saying — “O great king — Varuna’s ^ons are slain and the lord of waters, whom thou art inviting for battle, hath gone to the region of Brahma, to hear songs.

While the king is away, what is the use of taking trouble, O hero ? And all these heroic sons (of Vanina) have been vanquished.” Hearing these words and spreading his own name the lord of Rakshasas expressing sign of joy, issued out of Varuna’s abode. And returning by the way by which he had come, the Raksha, stationed in the welkin, proceeded towards Lanka.”

verses.sa:
ततो जित्वा दशग्रीवो यमं त्रिदशपुङ्गवम् ।
रावणस्तु रणश्लाघी स्वसहायान्ददर्श ह ॥

ततो रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गं प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतम् ।
रावणं राक्षसा दृष्ट्वा ह्यष्टवत् समुपागमन् ॥

जयेन वर्धयित्वा च मारीचप्रमुखास्ततः ।
पुष्पकं भेजिरे सर्वे सान्त्विता रावणेन तु ॥

ततो रसातलं गच्छन् प्रविष्टः पयसां निधिम् ।
दैत्योरगगणाध्युष्टं वरुणेन सुरक्षितम् ॥

स तु भोगवतीं गत्वा पुरीं वासुकिपालिताम् ।
कृत्वा नागान्वशे हृष्टो ययौ मणिमयीं पुरीम् ॥

निवातकवचास्तत्र दैत्या लब्धवरा वसन् ।
राक्षसान्तान्समागम्य युद्धाय समुपाह्वयत् ॥

ते तु सर्वे सुविक्रान्ता दैतेया बलशालिनः ।
नानाप्रहरणास्तत्र प्रहृष्टा युद्धदुर्मदाः ॥

शूलैस्त्रिशूलैः कुलिशैः पट्टिशासिपरश्वधैः ।
अन्योन्यं बिभिदुः क्रुद्धा राक्षसा दानवास्तथा ॥

तेषां तु युध्यमानानां साग्रः संवत्सरो गतः ।
न चान्यतरयोस्तत्र विजयो वा क्षयो ऽपि वा ॥

ततः पितामहस्तत्र त्रैलोक्यगतिरव्ययः ।
आजगाम द्रुतं देवो विमानवरमास्थितः ॥

निवातकवचानां तु निवार्य रणकर्म तत् ।
वृद्धः पितामहो वाक्यमुवाच विदितार्थवत् ॥

नह्ययं रावणो युद्धे शक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः ।
न भवन्तः क्षयं नेतुमपि सामरदानवैः ॥

राक्षसस्य सखित्वं च भवद्भिः सह रोचते ।
अविभक्ताश्च सर्वार्थाः सुहृदां नात्र संशयः ॥

ततो ऽग्निसाक्षिकं सख्यं कृतवांस्तत्र रावणः ।
निवातकवचैः सार्धं प्रीतिमानभवत्तदा ॥

अर्थतस्तैर्यथान्यायं संवत्सरमथोषितः ।
स्वपुरान्निर्विशेषं च प्रियं प्राप्तो दशाननः ॥

ततोपधार्य मायानां शतमेकं समाप्तवान् ।
सलिलेन्द्रपुरान्वेषी भ्रमति स्म रसातलम् ॥

ततो ऽश्मनगरं नाम कालकेयैरधिष्ठितम् ।
गत्वा तु कालकेयांश्च हत्वा तत्र बलोत्कटान् ॥

शूर्पणख्याश्च भर्तारमसिना प्राच्छिनत्तदा ।
श्यालं च बलवन्तं च विद्युज्जिह्वं बलोत्कटम् ।
जिह्वया संलिहन्तं च राक्षसं समरे तथा ॥
तं विजित्य मुहूर्तेन जघ्ने दैत्यांश्चतुःशतम् ॥

ततः पाण्डुरमेघाभं कैलासमिव भास्वरम् ।
वरुणस्यालयं दिव्यमपश्यद्राक्षसाधिपः ॥

क्षरन्तीं च पयस्तत्र सुरभिं गामवस्थिताम् ।
यस्याः पयोभिनिष्यन्दात्क्षीरोदो नाम सागरः ॥

ददर्श रावणस्तत्र गोवृषेन्द्रवरारणिम् ।
यस्माच्चन्द्रः प्रभवति शीतरश्मिर्निशाकरः ॥

यं समाश्रित्य जीवन्ति फेनपाः परमर्षयः ।
अमृतं यत्र चोत्पन्नं स्वधा च स्वधभोजिनाम् ॥

यां ब्रुवन्ति नरा लोके सुरभिं नाम नामतः ।
प्रदक्षिणं तु तां कृत्वा रावणः परमाद्भुताम् ॥

प्रविवेश महाघोरं गुप्तं बहुविधैर्बलैः ।
ततो धाराशताकीर्णं शारदाभ्रनिभं तदा ।
नित्यप्रहृष्टं ददृशे वरुणस्य गृहोत्तमम् ॥

ततो हत्वा बलाध्यक्षान्समरे तैश्च ताडितः ।
अब्रवीच्च ततो योधान्राजा शीघ्रं निवेद्यताम् ॥

युद्धार्थी रावणः प्राप्तस्तस्य युद्धं प्रदीयताम् ।
वद वा न भयं ते ऽस्ति निर्जितो ऽस्मीति साञ्जलिः ॥

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे क्रुद्धा वरुणस्य महात्मनः ।
पुत्राः पौत्राश्च निष्क्रामन्गौश्च पुष्कर एव च ॥

ते तु वीर्यगुणोपेता बलैः परिवृताः स्वकैः ।
युङ्क्त्वा रथान्कामगमानुद्यद्भास्वरवर्चसः ॥

ततो युद्धं समभवद्दारुणं रोमहर्षणम् ।
सलिलेन्द्रस्य पुत्राणां रावणस्य च धीमतः ॥

अमात्यैश्च महावीर्यैर्दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः ।
वारुणं तद्बलं कृत्स्नं क्षणेन विनिपातितम् ॥

समीक्ष्य स्वबलं सङ्ख्ये वरुणस्य सुतास्तदा ।
अर्दिताः शरजालेन निवृत्ता रणकर्मणः ॥

महीतलगतास्ते तु रावणं दृश्य पुष्पके ।
आकाशमाशु विविशुः स्यन्दनैः शीघ्रगामिभिः ॥

महादासीत्ततस्तेषां तुल्यं स्थानमवाप्य तत् ।
आकाशयुद्धं तुमुलं देवदानवयोरिव ॥

ततस्ते रावणं युद्धे शरैः पावकसन्निभैः ।
विमुखीकृत्य सन्तुष्टा विनेदुर्विविधान्रवान् ॥

ततो महोदरः क्रुद्धो राजानं दृश्य धर्षितम् ।
त्यक्त्वा मृत्युभयं वीरो युद्धकाङ्क्षी व्यलोकयत् ॥

तेन ते दारुणा युद्धे कामगाः पवनोपमाः ।
महोदरेण गदया हता वै प्रययुः क्षितिम् ॥

तेषां वरुणपुत्राणां हत्वा योधान्हयाञ्छतान् ।
मुमोचाशु महानादं विरथान्प्रेक्ष्य तान्स्थितान् ॥

ते तु तेषां रथाः साश्वाः सह सारथिभिर्हतैः ।
महोदरेण निहताः पतिताः पृथिवीतले ॥

ते तु त्यक्त्वा रथान्पुत्रा वरुणस्य महात्मनः ।
आकाशे विष्ठिताः शूराः स्वप्रभावान्न विव्यथुः ॥

धनूंषि कृत्वा सज्जानि विनिर्भिद्य महोदरम् ।
रावणं समरे क्रुद्धाः सहिताः समभिद्रवन् ॥

सायकैश्चापविभ्रष्टैर्वज्रकल्पैः सुदारुणैः ।
दारयन्ति स्म सङ्क्रुद्धा मेघा इव महागिरिम् ॥

ततः क्रुद्धो दशग्रीवः कालाग्निरिव निर्गतः ।
शरवर्षैर्महाघोरैस्तेषां मर्मस्वताडयत् ॥

ततस्तेनैव सहसा सीदन्ति स्म पदातयः ।
मुसलानि विचित्राणि ततो भल्लशतानि च ॥

पट्टिशांश्चैव शक्तीश्च शतघ्नीस्तोमरांस्तथा ।
पातयामास दुर्धर्षस्तेषामुपरि विष्ठितः ॥

अपविद्धास्तु ते वीरा विनिष्पेतुः पदातयः ।
महापङ्कमिवासाद्य कुञ्जराष्षष्टिहायनाः ॥

सीदमानान्सुतान्दृष्ट्वा विह्वलान्सुमहौजसः ।
ननाद रावणो हर्षान्महानम्बुधरो यथा ॥

ततो रक्षो महानादान्मुक्त्वा हन्ति स्म वारुणान् ।
नानाप्रहरणोपेतैर्धारापातैरिवाम्बुदः ॥

ततस्ते विमुखाः सर्वे पतिता धरणीतले ।
रणात्स्वपुरुषैः शीघ्रं गृहाण्येव प्रवेशिताः ॥
तानब्रवीत्ततो रक्षो वरुणाय निवेद्यताम् ॥

रावणं त्वब्रवीन्मन्त्री प्रहस्तो (प्रहसो) नाम वारुणः ।
गतः खलु महाराजो ब्रह्मलोकं जलेश्वरः ॥

गान्धर्वं वरुणः श्रोतुं यं त्वमाह्वयसे युधि ।
तत्किं तव वृथा वीर परिश्रम्य गते नृपे ।
ये तु सन्निहिता वीराः कुमारास्ते पराजिताः ॥

राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः ।
हर्षान्नादं विमुञ्चन्वै निष्क्रान्तो वरुणालयात् ॥

आगतस्तु पथा येन तेनैव विनिवृत्य सः ।
लङ्कामभिमुखो रक्षो नभस्तलगतो ययौ ॥
